issues.title: System discovery and relay bootstrap remain an unverified shared contract even though they gate every verified relay-backed slice
issues.summary: The current portfolio treats `/api/v1/system/info` as normative for public relay discovery, encrypted relay discovery, service pubkey discovery, and control-plane kind advertisement, but no completed PSTF slice yet verifies that contract directly as a first-class product feature.
evidence: `pstf/spec_gap_report.md` marks `/api/v1/system/info` and relay-read-model-first frontend behavior as high-risk missing specification areas.
`pstf/feature_backlog.md` ranks `SYSTEM_DISCOVERY_RELAY_BOOTSTRAP` first because every relay-backed browser flow depends on it.
`internal/api/handlers/system.go` emits `browser_relays`, `browser_encrypted_request_relays`, `sidecar_url`, `service_pubkey`, and control-plane kinds from the same payload.
Completed slices for core deployments, encrypted notifications, operator signer-first CLI discovery, and LLM all list `/api/v1/system/info` as a dependency or precondition.

recommended_actions.details: Promote this slice before broad release planning so the shared contract is verified once rather than assumed by downstream slices.
Add one contract test that proves the same `/api/v1/system/info` payload satisfies browser public bootstrap, browser encrypted transport gating, and operator CLI relay discovery.

issues.title: No cross-feature browser test proves mixed public and encrypted flows stay separated while sharing the same authenticated session and discovery payload
issues.summary: The portfolio has per-slice public and encrypted browser evidence, but no test proves that one browser session can bootstrap from one system-info contract, execute public signer-first flows and encrypted flows, and preserve the public-vs-encrypted relay boundary end to end.
evidence: `CORE_SERVICE_TO_DEPLOYMENT/verification_report.md` points to `service-deployment-public-smoke.spec.js` for the public browser journey.
`ENCRYPTED_CONTROL_PLANE_NOTIFICATIONS/verification_report.md` points to `notifications-encrypted-smoke.spec.js` and `notifications-form-error.spec.js` for encrypted browser journeys.
`LLM_ROUTE_RELEASE_DEPLOYMENT/verification_report.md` points to `llm-route-release-deployment.spec.js` for the dedicated `/llm` browser flow.
None of the verified reports records a combined browser scenario spanning both public and encrypted flows under one authenticated session and one discovery payload.
`pstf/spec_gap_report.md` explicitly calls the mixed transport model a high-risk area.

recommended_actions.details: Exercise one authenticated browser session that loads `/api/v1/system/info`, executes one public service/deployment or LLM command, executes one encrypted notifications command, and asserts the correct relay set is used for each flow.
Add explicit cross-slice boundary notes so public success evidence cannot silently stand in for encrypted separation evidence, or vice versa.

issues.title: Transport policy is fragmented across feature slices instead of being specified once as a shared portfolio rule
issues.summary: Each slice states its own transport boundary, but there is no single approved policy that defines when a browser flow must use public signer-first events, when it must use encrypted request/result transport, and when compatibility-only REST/NIP-98 fallback is acceptable.
evidence: `pstf/spec_gap_report.md` describes the mixed transport model as high-risk and explicitly calls public-vs-encrypted separation security-critical.

`web/src/lib/auth/route-access.js` contains route-level REST compatibility machinery, but `ROUTE_COMPATIBILITY_REQUIREMENTS` is empty, so the portfolio-level compatibility map is still implicit rather than explicit.
`CORE_SERVICE_TO_DEPLOYMENT/feature_spec.json` excludes encrypted request kind `5980` from the approved public deployment flow.
`ENCRYPTED_CONTROL_PLANE_NOTIFICATIONS/feature_spec.json` requires `browser_encrypted_request_relays` and forbids treating public relay URLs as encrypted request relays.
`SIGNER_FIRST_OPERATOR_ADOPTION_RUNTIME/feature_spec.json` permits explicit HTTP fallback only for pre-acceptance failures.
`LLM_ROUTE_RELEASE_DEPLOYMENT/hitl_decisions.md` removes operational REST mutations from the intended product contract.

recommended_actions.details: Decide whether Bahia needs a dedicated shared transport-policy slice now, or whether transport governance remains embedded per feature family.
If HITL chooses a shared rule, create a small slice that defines discovery, public signer-first, encrypted browser, and compatibility fallback boundaries once.

proposed_hitl_question.question: How should transport policy be governed across public browser flows, encrypted browser flows, and compatibility-only operator/browser fallback?
options: Create one dedicated shared transport-policy slice now and update dependent features to reference it
Keep transport policy embedded per feature slice
Standardize browser transport now, but keep operator fallback policy feature-specific
Defer and accept the current cross-feature transport-policy risk for this release

issues.title: Deployment run logs are a broken handoff between the verified public deployment journey and the encrypted transport family
issues.summary: The public deployment slice verifies the main deployment journey, but the deployment-detail run-log experience remains outside that slice and also outside the encrypted notifications slice. That leaves a user-visible deployment subflow without integrated acceptance coverage.
evidence: `CORE_SERVICE_TO_DEPLOYMENT/feature_spec.json` marks encrypted deployment run-log retrieval on `/deployments/runs/[id]` out of scope.
`CORE_SERVICE_TO_DEPLOYMENT/verification_report.md` recommends adding signer-first replacements for deployment run-log/detail browser coverage.
`pstf/feature_backlog.md` ranks `ENCRYPTED_DEPLOYMENT_RUN_LOGS` as a separate partially mapped feature candidate.
`internal/controlplane/encrypted_route_handlers.go` hosts encrypted route handlers for deployment run-log retrieval on the same transport family as other encrypted operations.

recommended_actions.details: Promote a bounded slice for encrypted run-log retrieval and rendering on the deployment detail journey.
Cover the handoff from public deployment history/detail to encrypted run-log retrieval in one deterministic browser scenario.

issues.title: Rollback policy is not standardized across deployment domains
issues.summary: Rollback is adjacent to both deployment domains, but one slice leaves rollback follow-up coverage for later and the other explicitly defers all rollback acceptance criteria because semantics are not approved. That makes rollback a portfolio-level policy gap, not only an LLM-local gap.
evidence: `LLM_ROUTE_RELEASE_DEPLOYMENT/hitl_decisions.md` records HITL-004 deferring all rollback acceptance criteria until replacement semantics are approved.
`LLM_ROUTE_RELEASE_DEPLOYMENT/feature_spec.json` keeps rollback in feature scope but classifies the current target-selection rule as FIX rather than intended behavior.
`CORE_SERVICE_TO_DEPLOYMENT/verification_report.md` recommends adding signer-first replacements for service-detail edit/delete/rollback in future coverage.

recommended_actions.details: Decide whether rollback semantics should be standardized across service deployments and LLM deployments, or remain domain-specific.
Use the HITL decision to determine whether to create one shared rollback-policy slice or separate domain-specific rollback follow-up slices.

proposed_hitl_question.question: How should rollback target-selection and user-visible semantics be handled across core service deployments and LLM deployments?
options: Standardize one rollback policy across both domains
Keep rollback domain-specific and verify each slice separately
Defer rollback standardization and create a dedicated rollback-policy slice
Exclude rollback from the current release train entirely until a policy is approved

issues.title: The promoted Hive-CI slice produces artifacts/build state consumed by deployments, but the handoff is still not end-to-end proven
issues.summary: Deployment-facing slices assume artifact/build availability, but the ingestion path that should populate that state is still called out as under-proven.
evidence: `pstf/spec_gap_report.md` states the selected CI-to-registry-to-artifact integration file is mostly scaffold and does not prove the flow end to end.
`pstf/backlog_decisions.md` records `HIVECI_RESULT_INGESTION_PIPELINE` as one of the promoted next slices.
`pstf/feature_backlog.md` describes the Hive-CI slice as the CI/OCI bridge into the build-artifact pipeline.

recommended_actions.details: Complete this promoted slice before claiming the artifact/build side of the deployment journey is portfolio-complete.
Add an integration scenario that proves CI result ingestion creates or enriches the artifact/build state that downstream deployment flows depend on.

issues.title: PSTF artifact refresh sequencing is inconsistent across the portfolio
issues.summary: At least one downstream artifact remained stale after later verification work, which means portfolio-level reporting can drift unless artifact refresh order is treated as a shared process rule.
evidence: `pstf/features/LLM_ROUTE_RELEASE_DEPLOYMENT/adversarial_review.json` still says no coverage artifact exists and recommends coverage generation.
`pstf/features/LLM_ROUTE_RELEASE_DEPLOYMENT/confidence_report.json` now records coverage artifacts and a 0.93 approved confidence score.
This is not a product bug, but it is a real process inconsistency in the PSTF artifact set.

recommended_actions.details: Document artifact refresh order for follow-up steps such as confidence and adversarial review so later evidence cannot leave stale contradictory reports behind.
Track this as process debt if product release planning is otherwise blocked by larger system issues.

shared_policy_gaps.title: System discovery contract governance
evidence: `/api/v1/system/info` is used by browser public bootstrap, browser encrypted gating, and CLI relay discovery.
No completed PSTF slice yet owns this contract directly.

shared_policy_gaps.title: Transport boundary governance
evidence: Per-slice transport boundaries exist, but no single shared transport policy is approved.
`route-access.js` has compatibility hooks with an empty compatibility map.

shared_policy_gaps.title: Rollback semantics governance
evidence: LLM rollback semantics are explicitly deferred.
Core deployment rollback remains future signer-first follow-up coverage.

candidate_cross_feature_tests.title: Single-session mixed transport journey
candidate_cross_feature_tests.description: In one authenticated browser session, bootstrap from `/api/v1/system/info`, execute one public signer-first command, execute one encrypted notification command, visit `/llm`, and assert public relay URLs are never used for encrypted requests while encrypted relay URLs are never used for public commands.

candidate_cross_feature_tests.title: System-info multi-consumer contract
candidate_cross_feature_tests.description: Use one canonical `/api/v1/system/info` fixture to prove browser public bootstrap, browser encrypted transport gating, LLM kind discovery, and CLI operator relay discovery all succeed without per-consumer divergence.

candidate_cross_feature_tests.title: Deployment history to encrypted run-log handoff
candidate_cross_feature_tests.description: Prove a user can traverse from the public deployment history/detail flow into encrypted run-log retrieval on a specific run without switching to a contradictory transport contract.

candidate_cross_feature_tests.title: Hive-CI ingestion to artifact-backed deploy
candidate_cross_feature_tests.description: Prove that subscribed Hive-CI result ingestion produces or enriches the artifact/build state that the deployment slice expects when creating an intent.

candidate_cross_feature_tests.title: Public signer-first requester policy consistency
candidate_cross_feature_tests.description: Verify that all public signer-first request families consistently subscribe before publish, require accepted relay OK responses, preserve correlation tags, and treat post-acceptance failures as terminal rather than fallback-eligible.

next_recommended_stage.summary: Before broad release planning, capture HITL decisions on shared transport policy and rollback governance, then promote `SYSTEM_DISCOVERY_RELAY_BOOTSTRAP` and `ENCRYPTED_DEPLOYMENT_RUN_LOGS`, and add at least one mixed-transport browser scenario plus one system-info multi-consumer contract test.
